title: Word Ladder II
statement:
A transformation sequence from word `beginWord` to word `endWord` using a dictionary `wordList` is a sequence of words `beginWord -> s1 -> s2 -> ... -> sk` such that:
- Every adjacent pair of words differs by a single letter.
- Every `si` for `1 <= i <= k` is in `wordList`.
- `sk == endWord`.

Return all the shortest transformation sequences from `beginWord` to `endWord`.
Print each sequence on a new line and sort the sequences lexicographically.
inputFormat:
Line 1: beginWord and endWord.
Line 2: an integer N (size of wordList).
Line 3: N space-separated strings.
outputFormat: Print all valid shortest paths, space-separated, lexicographically sorted.
constraints:
1 <= beginWord.length <= 10
endWord.length == beginWord.length
1 <= wordList.length <= 500
wordList[i].length == beginWord.length

examples.input:
hit cog
6
hot dot dog lot log cog
examples.output:
hit hot dot dog cog
hit hot lot log cog

starterCode.python:
beginWord, endWord = input().split()
n = int(input())
wordList = input().split()
# BFS for shortest paths graph, then DFS backtracking to build paths
